hypotheses.reasoning: The events-db data volume filled up. Disk usage on /var/lib/mysql hit 95% at 12:55 (#38) and 99% at 12:57 (#57), with WAL/binlog growing at 635 then 834MB/h. InnoDB writes then started failing with 'No space left on device' (#90, #101). As a direct result, ingest-api inserts failed with error 1114 'The table is full' (#91, #107), and ingest-gateway passed those back to clients as 500s on POST /v1/events. Reads don't need disk space, which is why they stayed healthy. Ruled out: enrichment-svc responded fine the whole time (~60-90ms), I found no deploy in the logs, and there were no other errors or warnings anywhere before the disk warnings.
Binlog growth sped up, so binlog retention or purge settings may be misconfigured. That would explain why the disk filled, but the logs don't show any config change.

verdict.recommendedAction: Free space on events-db now: purge old binary logs (PURGE BINARY LOGS) or grow the /var/lib/mysql volume, then confirm inserts succeed again. After that, find out why binlog/WAL growth sped up (retention settings, a replica that has stopped reading binlogs), set binlog_expire_logs_seconds, and add disk alerts that fire before usage reaches 90%.
